commit 54d30d4b795727d2b1028df5be27d1e9e.message:
Cherry pick #38861 to release-11.7 (#39258)

* [MM-69775] Delete the server-side draft when sending from the Drafts panel (#38861)

* MM-69775: Delete the server draft when sending from the Drafts panel

Sending a draft from the Drafts panel only cleared the locally stored
copy: createPost dispatches storeDraft(null), which is a setGlobalItem
and never reaches Client4.deleteDraft. The server draft survived and
getDrafts restored it on the next team switch or reload.

The channel composer is unaffected because its handleDraftChange sees
the emptied draft after submit and dispatches removeDraft, which does
delete the server copy.

afterSubmit now calls handleOnDelete for a plain send as well as for a
scheduled one, leaving the scheduled-post send path untouched.

Co-authored-by: mattermost-code <matty-code@mattermost.com>

* MM-69775: Cover the Drafts panel send path with real submit wiring

draft_row.test.tsx mocked useSubmit outright, so nothing exercised what
DraftRow does after a post is created. The mock is gone and the action
rows are now interactive fakes that invoke the real callbacks, so the
tests run through useSubmit, onSubmit, createPost and afterSubmit and
assert on the requests Client4 actually receives.

Covers a plain channel send, a thread send, scheduling, sending a
scheduled post, and both failure paths.

Co-authored-by: mattermost-code <matty-code@mattermost.com>

* MM-69775: Add E2E coverage for sending a draft from the Drafts panel

Both specs assert the server draft list is empty after the send, which
is the invariant the bug broke; the UI assertions alone could not see it
for the thread case. Reverting the draft_row fix fails both specs on
that assertion.

DraftsPage gains the Send message now modal and a sendDraft helper,
mirroring ScheduledPostsPage.

Co-authored-by: mattermost-code <matty-code@mattermost.com>

* MM-69775: Drop the now-dead isBeingScheduled ref and sharpen the tests

afterSubmit no longer branches on isBeingScheduled, which left the ref
written in two places and read in none, so it is gone.

Test changes come from a review pass that found three assertions which
passed with the fix reverted:
- the drafts-list assertion is now driven by a fake server draft table
  that deleteDraft mutates and getUserDrafts serves back, with a real
  getDrafts refetch, so it reproduces the reported symptom
- the create-failure test became a pending-promise test, since a
  rejected createPost never reaches afterSubmit; it now pins that the
  delete waits for the created post instead of firing on click
- the scheduled-post test also asserts the live channel draft survives,
  which kills a keepDraft flip, and sends twice
- the Playwright thread test dropped its post-reload assertions, which
  could not fail for this bug, and says what it actually proves

Co-authored-by: mattermost-code <matty-code@mattermost.com>

* MM-69775: Assert the scheduled draft leaves the panel, not just the server

Scheduling returns before createPost, so handleOnDelete is the only
thing that clears the local copy on that path. Asserting only on
deleteDraft's arguments let a wrong storage key survive: the server
delete still looked right while the row stayed in the Drafts panel.

Also assert the fake server draft table itself shrank after a plain
send, so a degraded fixture cannot quietly weaken that test.

Co-authored-by: mattermost-code <matty-code@mattermost.com>

* MM-69775: Tighten comments across the change

Drops comments that restated the assertion on the following line, keeps
the ones carrying facts the code cannot show, and matches the comment
style of each surrounding file.

commit 60ecc27b9c0bf4a2bc008adbb67da7a6a.message:
fix(e2e): repoint markdown image tests off the deleted docs.mattermost.com asset (#38330) (#38567)

docs.mattermost.com migrated from Sphinx to Docusaurus, which removed the
/_images/ static path. https://docs.mattermost.com/_images/icon-76x76.png now
returns 404, so the image proxy fails and the webapp renders the broken-image
placeholder instead. That breaks four specs on every run, independent of the
change under test:

  - markdown/markdown_image_spec.js "with in-line images 1"
  - messaging/inline_markdown_image_link_open_link_spec.js MM-T188
  - files_and_attachments/image_link_preview_spec.js MM-T2389
  - fixtures/markdown/markdown_inline_images_1.md

The icon is gone from the docs site entirely (no /img/, /static/img/,
/img/brand/ or /assets/images/ equivalent), so point these at an image we
actually own: the in-repo fixture mattermost-icon_128x128.png, served over
raw.githubusercontent.com. That is the convention several sibling specs
already use, and it removes the dependency on the docs site's asset layout.

Size assertions move from 76px to 128px to match the new fixture. 128px stays
under the 350px max-height cap on .markdown-inline-img, so the image still
renders at its natural size. The height tolerance tightens from closeTo(76, 76)
- which accepted anything from 0 to 152 and would have passed on a
zero-height broken image - to closeTo(128, 2).

(cherry picked from commit 86088592790eb63047bee73cd82390aae0c3e27b)

Co-authored-by: Angelos Kyratzakos <angelos.kyratzakos@mattermost.com>

commit aee40c775a16cc933ea36f9f430f35585.message:
E2E/Playwright: fix upgrade-to swap resolving the wrong image in workers (release-11.11) (#39180)

* E2E/Playwright: fix upgrade-to swap resolving the wrong image in workers

TestConfig recomputed serverImage via reloadTestConfig() during the
upgrade swap, but isUpgradeToPhaseProjectSelected() only checked argv,
which workers never inherit. The swap worker fell back to the
persisted from-image instead of SERVER_IMAGE, so the swap left the
from-image running and failed assertRunningContainerImage(). The same
argv-only gap also made mattermostWaitStrategy() skip the migration
log wait for the swap's restart.

Add isUpgradeFromProjectActive()/isUpgradeToPhaseProjectActive(),
worker-safe (env-var-aware) versions used by test_config.ts,
mattermost_container.ts, and stack.ts. Keep the argv-only originals
for playwright.config.ts's one-time preflight checks, which must not
re-trigger inside a dependency project's worker (e.g. upgrade-from's
setup dependency).

Co-authored-by: saturnino <saturnino@mattermost.com>

* E2E/Playwright: make isUpgradePathProjectSelected() worker-safe

This branch's upgrade_env.ts predates master's worker-safe
isUpgradePathProjectSelected() (it still only checked argv), so
resetConfigAndRoles' 'skip resetRoles() during an upgrade-path project'
guard in test_fixture.ts silently failed open in worker processes
(workers don't inherit --project). Mirror master: UPGRADE_PATH_PROJECT_ENV
env var, isUpgradePathProjectSelected() also checks it, and the export
function (renamed exportUpgradePathProjectSelection() to match) sets it
alongside the existing from/to-phase env vars.

Verified locally with testcontainers: upgrade-from (release-11.10) ->
upgrade-to (release-11.11), 3 full cycles, 10/10 tests passing each run.

Co-authored-by: saturnino <saturnino@mattermost.com>

commit c16c8db24f73cd3f5ade8c2ce01bdf3aa.message:
MM-70595: Enforce log path root behind a feature flag (#38634) (#39192)

* MM-70595: Enforce log path root behind a feature flag

Log and audit file paths resolving outside the logging root (MM_LOG_PATH,
or the default logs directory) were only logged as an error on config save,
and were never checked at startup at all. Two of the four relevant fields
were not checked even once.

Add the EnforceLogPathRoot feature flag, disabled by default:

  - disabled: the path is logged as an error, as before
  - enabled:  the server refuses to start, and a config save that introduces
              such a path is rejected with HTTP 400

Enforcement is a breaking change for deployments with log paths outside the
root and no MM_LOG_PATH set, and was never announced, so it stays opt-in.
The default flips once every supported release carries the flag.

WarnIfLogPathsOutsideRoot is replaced by config.ValidateLogPaths, which
returns an error for the first offending path and knows nothing about the
flag; each caller decides what to do with it. Coverage now spans all four
fields: LogSettings.FileLocation, LogSettings.AdvancedLoggingJSON,
ExperimentalAuditSettings.FileName and
ExperimentalAuditSettings.AdvancedLoggingJSON.

The gate lives in initLogging, before ConfigureLogger opens any target, so
it also covers config reload (which bypasses SaveConfig) and the audit
logger (configured later in the boot sequence). On reload the previously
configured targets are left in place.

Also fix ValidateLogFilePath, which resolved symlinks on the file path but
not on the root. A root containing a symlinked component (/var on macOS, a
symlinked mount) therefore rejected every path inside it, which would block
startup once enforcement is on. Both sides now resolve the deepest existing
ancestor, which additionally catches a symlinked parent directory pointing
out of the root for a not-yet-created file.

* Prevent log path disclosure in config save errors

Log validation details server-side, keep API errors generic, update regression assertions, and clarify that enforcement applies to all System Console config saves.

* Fix check-style and the empty log path save error

mattermost-govet's errorAssertions analyzer rejects assert.Nil on an error,
and AppError.Unwrap returns one:

  config_test.go:248:3: calling assert.Nil on error, please use assert.NoError instead

Switch to assert.NoError.

The same change made the AppError generic by dropping its i18n params, but
the translation still interpolated {{.Error}}, so an admin saw the literal
"Invalid logging configuration: <no value>". Replace it with a static
message that keeps the path out of the API response and points at the
server log, where the offending path is now recorded.

* Mention audit paths in the log path save error

ValidateLogPaths checks ExperimentalAuditSettings.FileName and
ExperimentalAuditSettings.AdvancedLoggingJSON alongside the LogSettings
fields, so the save error can be triggered by an audit path alone. Say
"log or audit file path" rather than "log file path".

* Treat advanced logging file target types case-insensitively

logr lowercases target types before building them, so EqualFold is needed
to keep EnforceLogPathRoot from being bypassed with mixed-case "file".

* Rename resolveSymlinkPath to make its missing-path behavior explicit

* Add EnforceLogPathRoot to generated files, support packet golden and i18n description

---------

Co-authored-by: coderabbitai[bot] <136622811+coderabbitai[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>

pull 38634.body:
#### Summary

Log and audit file paths that resolve outside the logging root (`MM_LOG_PATH`, or the default `logs` directory) were only logged as an error on config save, and were never validated at startup at all. Two of the four relevant fields were not validated even once.

This adds the **`EnforceLogPathRoot` feature flag, disabled by default**:

| Flag | Behavior |
|---|---|
| **off** (default) | the offending path is logged as an error, as today |
| **on** | the server refuses to start, and a config save that introduces such a path is rejected with HTTP 400 |

Enforcement is a breaking change for deployments that have log paths outside the root and no `MM_LOG_PATH` set, and it was never announced — the old "will fail to start in a future version" wording lived only in a code comment and one log line. So it stays opt-in for now. The default flips once every supported release carries the flag.

**Validation is now centralized.** `WarnIfLogPathsOutsideRoot` is replaced by `config.ValidateLogPaths`, which returns an error for the first offending path and knows nothing about the flag — each caller decides what to do with it. Coverage now spans all four fields:

- `LogSettings.FileLocation` *(previously validated on the read path only)*
- `LogSettings.AdvancedLoggingJSON`
- `ExperimentalAuditSettings.FileName` *(previously not validated at all)*
- `ExperimentalAuditSettings.AdvancedLoggingJSON`

**The gate lives in `initLogging`, before `ConfigureLogger` opens any target.** T

```release-note
Added the EnforceLogPathRoot feature flag, disabled by default. When enabled, a log or audit file path that resolves outside the logging root (MM_LOG_PATH, or the default logs directory) causes the server to refuse to start and is rejected on configuration save, instead of only being logged as an error. Validation now also covers LogSettings.FileLocation and ExperimentalAuditSettings.FileName.
```

pull 38861.body:
#### Summary

Sending a synced draft from the Drafts panel left the server copy alive, so the draft came back on the next team switch or reload.

`DraftRow`'s `afterSubmit` only called `handleOnDelete()` when the draft was being **scheduled**. For a plain send the only clearing was `storeDraft(post.channel_id, null)` inside `createPost` (`actions/post_actions.ts`), which is a local `setGlobalItem` and never reaches `Client4.deleteDraft`. The server draft survived and `getDrafts` restored it on the next fetch.

The channel composer is unaffected because its real `handleDraftChange` sees the emptied draft after submit and dispatches `removeDraft`, which does delete the server copy. `DraftRow` passes `noop` for `handleDraftChange`, so nothing covered it there.

`afterSubmit` now returns early unless the post was created, handles the scheduled-post send first, and otherwise calls `handleOnDelete()` for both a plain send and a scheduled one. That made `isBeingScheduled` write-only, so the ref is removed.

The fix is 16 lines in one file; the rest of the diff is tests.

**Deliberately not changed:** `isScheduledPostBeingSent` could be replaced by the derived `isScheduledPost`, and the local clear still races between `removeDraft`'s empty draft and `createPost`'s `null` (both are filtered identically by `makeGetDraftsByPrefix`, so it is not user visible). Neither is caused by this fix, so both are left alone.

**Follow-up worth filing:** the Retry link on a failed post (`components/

```release-note
Fixed an issue where a draft sent from the Drafts panel could reappear after switching teams or reloading.
```

#### Summary
Follow-up to #39003, which fixed up config values that started fine before v12 but fail v12's stricter validation.

**Unusable email settings no longer stop the server.** #39003 removed display names from `SupportSettings.SupportEmail`, `EmailSettings.FeedbackEmail` and `EmailSettings.ReplyToAddress`. A value that didn't parse as one address, like a list or a bare name, still failed startup with `model.config.is_valid.email_address.app_error`. Now:
- A comma-separated address list is reduced to its first address, if that address is valid.
- Anything else is cleared, since email sent with it before v12 was already broken.

In both cases a warning logs the setting and its old value.

**`mattermost db` subcommands now load translations before the config.** `db migrate`, `db init`, `db downgrade`, `db reset` and `db version` loaded the config before loading translations. As a result:
- A validation error printed its raw message ID, without naming the setting.
- The locale check warned that `en` wasn't a supported locale.

They now load translations first, like `mattermost server` does.

pull 39323.body:
#### Summary
Fixes an endless DB query loop in `RemoveNotifications` when a deleted thread reply mentions two or more groups.

The paging loop for each group's members stopped when `len(userIDs) == count`. `userIDs` is shared across all mentioned groups, but `count` is a single group's member count. Once an earlier group had added users, a later group could never reach that condition and kept requesting empty pages in a tight loop, so each such delete left a stuck goroutine querying the DB until restart. A later group could also stop early at a page boundary and skip members' unread-mention cleanup.

Each group's loop now counts its own users and stops once it reaches that group's `count`, or on an empty page in case membership changes while paging.

Two regression tests were added to `TestRemoveNotifications`:
- Two groups with members in the channel. Before the fix, `RemoveNotifications` never returned.
- Groups of 50 and 150 members, which hit the page boundary. Before the fix, 50 members kept their unread mention.
